summary:
Brazil’s presidential election will be decided in a runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro led incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round. Bolsonaro won about 47% of the vote, short of the majority needed to win outright, and the runoff is scheduled for 25 October. In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for 29 November after parliament rejected two emergency measures addressing the housing crisis, adding to the difficulties faced by his minority coalition.

Yemen’s internationally recognized government announced a military campaign to retake territory held by the Houthis. The announcement followed rebel gains and the cutting of a key road between Taiz and Aden. In France, student protests over school conditions, overcrowding and teacher shortages disrupted classes at hundreds of high schools; authorities said up to 500 would close fully or partly, with more demonstrations planned for Tuesday.

Gulf crude exports returned to pre-war levels in September despite attacks around the Strait of Hormuz, as producers relied more on alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers. Iranian exports remain below their pre-war average. The United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain a week after five men were arrested nearby on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts; the BBC reported that no reason had been given. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, an Ebola outbreak has become the country’s worst. Africa CDC supports the government’s efforts to strengthen transparency and accountability in response funding.

headlines.title: Brazil’s presidential race heads to a runoff
headlines.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro led incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s first-round presidential vote, but neither won a majority. The runoff is scheduled for 25 October; Bolsonaro received about 47% of the vote.

headlines.title: Spain calls snap election after housing measures fail
headlines.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early election after parliament rejected two emergency housing measures. The vote is scheduled for 29 November, following defeats that exposed difficulties for his minority coalition.

headlines.title: Yemen’s government launches offensive against Houthis
headlines.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognized government announced a military campaign to retake territory held by the Houthis. The announcement followed rebel gains and the cutting of a key road linking Taiz with Aden.

headlines.title: Student protests disrupt hundreds of French schools
headlines.summary: Student demonstrations over school conditions, overcrowding and teacher shortages have disrupted classes across France. Authorities said up to 500 high schools would close fully or partly, with more protests planned for Tuesday.

headlines.title: Middle East oil exports recover to pre-war levels
headlines.summary: Gulf crude exports returned to pre-war levels in September despite attacks around the Strait of Hormuz. Producers have increasingly used alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers, while Iranian exports remain below their pre-war average.

headlines.title: US removes B-1 bombers from British air base
headlines.summary: The United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain. The move came a week after five men were arrested nearby on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts; the BBC said no reason for the withdrawal had been given.

headlines.title: Congo Ebola outbreak becomes the country’s worst
headlines.summary: An outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the worst the country has seen, with conditions in Mangala contributing to its rapid spread. Africa CDC says it supports the government’s efforts to strengthen transparency and accountability in response funding.
